solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Took in bitter liquid

indicators.note: 'took in' read as something taken inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: wry humour has a bitter, twisted edge
took food, past tense of eat

explanation.surface: Someone swallowed a sour drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took in' reads as one verb, but 'Took' gives the filler and 'in' places it inside the bitter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery describes something thin and fluid, much like a liquid state rather than solid.

clue.text: Always a 100% pass rate

definitions.note: cryptic: a record with no failures in it

blocks.note: first meaning: every time, invariably
second meaning, read literally: a record containing no failures at all

explanation.walkthrough: The second part reads like a school's exam boast; taken literally it describes something lacking any failure.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means reliably every time, and a perfect pass rate has literally no failures in it.

clue.text: Sportsman arrested, he hates raising temperature: conclusion of case for acquittal

indicators.note: someone arrested is held, so this word is held within the others
in a down entry raising a letter moves it higher, so it changes position earlier in the word

blocks.note: taken as written
to detest is to hate
T is the abbreviation for temperature
a fencer is a sportsman who duels with swords

explanation.surface: A detained athlete gets heated, hating the court case that ends in his acquittal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry raising a letter moves it upwards, so the T jumps to the top of the hating phrase before the sportsman is held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Defence counsel say this formula in court to signal they have finished presenting their side.

clue.text: Claim bank swaps tips about Sunday Special

indicators.note: two words exchanging their tips trade their leading letters with each other

blocks.note: to boast is to claim proudly
a reef is a bank of rock or sand in the sea

explanation.surface: A bank's claims department trades advice about a Sunday newspaper special.
explanation.walkthrough: The tips here are the first letters, which trade places between the two words. Roast beef is the classic British Sunday lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional British Sunday lunch centres on a joint of roasted meat from cattle.

clue.text: Truant’s bagged 3ft jumper

indicators.note: to have bagged something is to hold it in a bag, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a skiver is British slang for someone who dodges school or work
three feet make a yard, abbreviated YD

explanation.surface: A child skipping school has stolen a three-foot sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is British for a sweater, which is the surface reading; here it is someone who jumps from aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A skydiver leaps out of planes for sport, making them literally someone who jumps.

clue.text: Long ready to fight for core of family growth area

indicators.note: 'for' means in place of, so new letters replace the central one of the word

blocks.note: kin are family
to long for is to itch for
en garde is the fencing call to take guard, ready to fight

explanation.surface: An ambitious relative is spoiling for a fight over the family business's growth area.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle I of KIN is replaced by ITCH plus EN GARDE. 'Growth area' sounds like business jargon but means where vegetables grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot where household vegetables and herbs are cultivated is literally a place for plants to grow.

clue.text: King agreed to go around northern butcher’s

indicators.note: in a down entry going north means travelling upwards, so the word is read bottom to top
going around something encloses it

blocks.note: OK'd means agreed
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king consents to visit a butcher's shop up north.
explanation.walkthrough: A butcher's is cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look. Reversed OKED is DEKO, which goes around K.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a quick glance, the rhyming slang and the Hindi-derived word.

clue.text: Politician cryptically after very important data

indicators.note: written cryptically suggests a special typeface, so the word sits inside the slanted print's name
after means the next piece follows the one named

blocks.note: v is the abbreviation for very
a statist is a politician favouring state control
the politician is written in italics, a slanted type

explanation.surface: A politician cryptically chases very important data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptically' is used as a typeface joke: the politician is written slanted. 'Very important' wants to stay together; very is just V.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers key figures such as population numbers, and jokingly a person's body measurements.

clue.text: Right on, I get this cheer

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it, coming first

blocks.note: R abbreviates right
'ah' is what you say when you understand something

explanation.surface: Someone shouts 'Right on!' and says they get the applause.
explanation.definitionFit: The short exclamation is a shout of encouragement, as in rah-rah supporters cheering a team.

clue.text: “Passed on” etc knowing cracking distillate decays sailing boat

indicators.note: one word cracking another breaks into it and ends up lodged in the middle

blocks.note: tar is distilled from wood or coal
hep is old slang for in the know
rots means decays
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A list of jargon about a knowing, boozy liquid and decaying boats.
explanation.walkthrough: The Monty Python sketch has John Cleese listing euphemisms for a dead bird: 'passed on', 'ceased to be' and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous comedy routine about a dead bird strings together euphemisms like 'passed on', so the quote plus etc evokes it.

clue.text: Apoplectic prison officer leaves employment prickling with fury

indicators.note: someone apoplectic is beside themselves with rage, so the word is thrown into disorder
leaves means departs, so the letters of the following word go out of the one before

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
an office is a post or employment
tingly means prickling

explanation.surface: An enraged prison officer quits his job, prickling with fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking OFFICE out of OFFICER leaves just R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rip-snorting means wildly boisterous or furious, so doing something this way is with violent energy.

clue.text: Straightforward, inherently honest, epitaph

indicators.note: inherently means within by nature, so the letters lie inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A gravestone inscription that is plain and truthful.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-step process is simple and direct, requiring only a single stage to complete.

clue.text: Rowdy, grating loud-mouthed duet shown the way out

indicators.note: someone shown the way out is ejected, so those letters leave the fodder
grating suggests scraping and shredding, so the remaining letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; its four letters are removed

explanation.surface: A noisy pair of singers is thrown out of the venue for their grating voices.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing D, U, E and T from the loud word leaves LOMOUHD, which is rearranged. 'Rowdy' looks like an adjective but is the noun, a rowdy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy as a noun is a rough troublemaker, which a hoodlum, a young thug, also is.

clue.text: Amount raised by college to check my postural aids

indicators.note: in a down entry raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a sum is an amount
C abbreviates college
a let is a check or hindrance, as in 'without let'
one's is the impersonal form of my

explanation.surface: A college raises money to monitor my posture supports.
explanation.walkthrough: SUM reversed gives MUS, followed by C, LET and ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: The steady tension in muscles keeps the body upright, so it supports good posture.

clue.text: They make Northern Division again, with record breaking baseball teams

indicators.note: breaking into a word means splitting it and sitting in the gap

blocks.note: then can mean besides or again, as in 'and then there's'
an EP is an extended-play record
a baseball team fields nine players, so teams are nines

explanation.surface: Planners redraw the north while baseball teams smash records.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pennines are the hill range running down northern England, often called its backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: This upland chain splits northern England into east and west halves, so the hills form a natural divide.

clue.text: Perversely accepts Lorde at Fringe show

indicators.note: a fringe is the edge, so only the word's border letters are used
perversely means contrarily, against the normal order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the outer two letters of the singer's name

explanation.surface: The pop singer Lorde unexpectedly agrees to play the Edinburgh Fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Fringe is a huge arts festival, which makes 'Fringe show' look like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is an impressive public display or performance, which is what a show is.

clue.text: I can confirm poet’s notes

definitions.note: a poetic contraction used to affirm, 'it is so'
plural noun, matched by the plural of a sol-fa note

blocks.note: first meaning: the poetic contraction of 'it is', said to agree
second meaning: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, and these are several of it

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for a poet's jottings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like written jottings; it is musical notes of the do-re-mi scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Poets write the short form of 'it is' to agree with something, and ti is a tonic sol-fa syllable whose plural matches.

clue.text: It’s easy rating clubs

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for something easy, as in 'easy as this'

blocks.note: an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
C abbreviates clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Someone says a review score for golf clubs is simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating' suggests a score; in crosswords it is a sailor below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as easy as ABC' makes the alphabet's first letters a byword for simplicity.

clue.text: Heavenly Father is half taken in by mother of Psyche

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word keeps just one of its letters, here the leading one
something taken in by another is held inside it

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for a priest, Father
the first half of the word
ma is a familiar word for mother
psyche means the mind, and mental means of the mind

explanation.surface: Mythology: the Heavenly Father is partly absorbed by the mother of the goddess Psyche.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital P makes Psyche look like the mythical goddess; it is just the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the sky, so anything pertaining to it is celestial.

clue.text: German seductress learning Romanian’s ready

blocks.note: lore is accumulated learning
the leu, plural lei, is Romania's currency, and ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: A German temptress picks up the language and is prepared for a Romanian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like an adjective, but 'the ready' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: In Rhine legend a siren of that name sang from a rock and lured boatmen to their deaths.

clue.text: Invention in position

definitions.note: a noun: the act of telling untruths
an adjective phrase: placed, as in 'lying third'

blocks.note: first meaning: making things up, telling falsehoods
second meaning: situated or placed, as a team in a league table

explanation.definitionFit: Telling untruths is fabrication, and a horse or team placed somewhere in the standings is said to be there.

clue.text: Deposit on return of a little file

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the phrase is read backwards

blocks.note: 'a tad' means a little
to set something down is to deposit it

explanation.surface: A bank deposit made on getting a small refund back.
explanation.walkthrough: In a charade 'on' puts the first piece after the second, so SET follows the reversed A TAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dataset is a collection of records stored together, in effect a computer document.

clue.text: North Acton perhaps unaccounted for by dispatch office?

definitions.note: a cryptic sense: the phrase written N ACTON lacks one letter of a longer word

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: N plus ACTON is a word for a deed lacking its I
second meaning: the military phrase for a soldier not found after battle

explanation.surface: Someone from a London suburb has gone astray in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: North Acton is a district of west London. Read cryptically it is N ACT ON, which is missing I + N + ACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: War office dispatches list soldiers whose fate is unknown after combat under this official phrase.

clue.text: Catcall divided IOW?

indicators.note: dividing the capitalised group splits off its first two letters as a name, which is then swapped for the pronoun it stands for

blocks.note: taken as written, then split into IO and W; Io is the setter, who would call themselves me

explanation.surface: Jeering at someone over a split of the Isle of Wight.
explanation.walkthrough: IOW is the abbreviation for the Isle of Wight, an island off southern England; split it as IO plus W, and Io is this puzzle's setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's call is its cry, the high thin sound a kitten makes.

clue.text: Mafiosi hearing questions form

indicators.note: on hearing something you take in its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: whys are questions
a guise is an outward form

explanation.surface: Mob members at a court hearing fill in a questionnaire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests a trial, apt for gangsters, but it signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang calls members of organised crime families by this name.

clue.text: Opposing recital of poetry

indicators.note: a recital is spoken or performed out loud, so only the pronunciation matters

blocks.note: poetry is written in verses

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a poetry reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin preposition means against, used for sides opposed in a contest or lawsuit.
